channel.title: Bola Pádel
channel.description: Bola Pádel: pro padel tour news, opinion, podcast and a weekly newsletter.

item.title: Aimar Goñi will play his first Major semifinal before heading to the World Cup with Spain
item.description: With Edu Alonso, 6-1, 6-2 against Stupaczuk and Sanz, the fourth seeds. Today, in Kuwait, against Tello and Arce. Next week, Goñi plays the World Cup.

item.title: Libaak and Alfonso beat Lebrón and Augsburger again and will face Di Nenno and Navarro
item.description: They had already beaten them in Madrid. Yesterday, in Kuwait, they did it again: in the third set, Lebrón and Augsburger won just one game. Sintes and Zamora are also into the quarterfinals. Yanguas and Nieto are out.

item.title: Lebrón and Augsburger beat Abud and Belluati and will face Libaak and Alfonso
item.description: The qualifiers' run is over. Coello and Tapia, in under an hour, and Yanguas and Nieto, in three sets, are also into the round of 16. Today, Augsburger faces his national team partner.

item.title: Sintes and Zamora beat Momo and Campagnolo and will play their first Major round of 16
item.description: Between them they are 38 years old. They were one game from losing and won the next three. On Wednesday, in Kuwait, they play their first round of 16 at a Major.

item.title: Abud and Belluati come back in Kuwait and will face Lebrón and Augsburger
item.description: They came through qualifying, lost the first set and turned it around. It's Martín Abud's first main-draw win at a Major. On Tuesday, the third seeds.

item.title: Chingotto and Galán pull out of the Kuwait Major after an injury to Ale Galán
item.description: Ale Galán is injured and the second-ranked pair won't play in Kuwait. The very place where, a year ago, they won the first FIP World Cup Pairs.

item.title: Hexagon leaves Madrid: four venues, eight teams and goodbye to sets
item.description: The Hexagon Cup becomes the Hexagon World Series. In 2027 it starts in Madrid and ends in Abu Dhabi, with eight teams and a format with no games or sets: best of five super tie-breaks.

item.title: These are Argentina's 16 for the World Cup in Qatar
item.description: Eight men and eight women. The men are defending the title and going for a third in a row. The women want revenge after two finals lost to Spain.

item.title: These are Spain's 16 for the World Cup in Qatar
item.description: Eight men and eight women. From 2 to 7 November, in Doha. The men want back a title they haven't won since 2021. The women are going for a seventh in a row.

item.title: Augsburger and Libaak launch their own brand with Siux
item.description: Two Argentinians from Siux, two new logos in one week. Leo Augsburger now signs as "Laugsburger". Tino Libaak does it with three letters: TLK.

item.title: Coello and Tapia come back in Milan: three titles in three weeks
item.description: They dropped the first set to Augsburger and Lebrón and won 4-6, 6-3, 6-2. In the women's final, Ari Sánchez and Andrea Ustero beat Josemaría and González again: 7-6, 6-3.

item.title: Augsburger and Lebrón: from 0-6 to the Milan final
item.description: They lost the first set without winning a game against Galán and Chingotto. Then they took twelve of the remaining sixteen.

item.title: Coello and Tapia complete the double: Rotterdam and Düsseldorf
item.description: Two P2s in two weeks. Two finals against Stupaczuk and Sanz. Two titles.

item.title: Martina Calvo and Claudia Fernández win in Düsseldorf
item.description: No contest in the final against Ari Sánchez and Andrea Ustero: 6-3, 6-0 in one hour and six minutes.
